instruction.name: x86srai.d
instruction.description: x86-style arithmetic shift right by immediate on 64-bit values.

latencies.notes: Slope method (--unroll 100000, --unroll2 200000), median of three runs; 1 cycles of flag-helper latency subtracted where the chain closes through x86mtflag/x86mfflag. Measured on 2026-11-17 on LA464, core 0.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: x86srai.d $r12, 1; x86srai.d $r13, 1; x86srai.d $r14, 1; x86srai.d $r15, 1; x86srai.d $r16, 1; x86srai.d $r17, 1; x86srai.d $r18, 1; x86srai.d $r19, 1
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'x86mtflag $r0, 1' --asm 'x86srai.d $r12, 1; x86srai.d $r13, 1; x86srai.d $r14, 1; x86srai.d $r15, 1; x86srai.d $r16, 1; x86srai.d $r17, 1; x86srai.d $r18, 1; x86srai.d $r19, 1'
throughput.notes: The instruction writes no general-purpose register, so the 8 lanes differ in their source registers and each one retires an EFLAGS write; 16.00 cycles for 8 instructions is the flag-write throughput, 2 CPI (0.5 IPC).

notes: Only EFLAGS is written: the general-purpose registers are read-only sources for this instruction (verified with a native test program, where every GPR keeps its value after execution while EFLAGS changes as documented, e.g. x86sub.b of 6 and 7 sets CF, SF, PF and AF).
